SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/audit-center

# Audit Integration Reference

This reference defines how software, registries, and diligence workflows consume Whale CeFi audit evidence without turning a report title into an unsupported assurance claim.

## Canonical record

The machine-readable source is [audits.json](../data/audits.json). Each audit record identifies:

- auditor and exact scope;
- report version and issue date;
- repository, commit, package, or deployed bytecode covered;
- immutable artifact hash;
- finding totals by severity and original auditor status;
- remediation commits and regression tests;
- independent retest artifact;
- deployment IDs that inherit the reviewed code;
- exclusions, expiry, and superseding review.

The public [Audit Center](../evidence-center/audit-center.md) is the reader-facing explanation. This page is the integration contract.

## Finding lifecycle

`reported → triaged → remediation-linked → regression-tested → independently-retested → deployment-bound`

An internal closure state never overwrites the original report. “Acknowledged,” “fixed,” “verified,” and “covered by the deployed version” remain separate fields.

## Consumer rules

1. Reject a record whose artifact hash, scope, code identity, or issue date is missing.
2. Do not extend review coverage to a contract, service, chain, proxy, implementation, or deployment that is absent from scope.
3. Treat a remediation without independent retest as remediated-but-unverified.
4. Resolve proxy and implementation addresses before displaying deployment coverage.
5. Preserve superseded records for history while presenting the latest applicable record first.
6. Fail closed when the audit record and deployment registry disagree.

## Current assurance set

The target-state registry names **Eter** and **Hashlock**. Auditor-issued files, hashes, exact finding statuses, and covered deployment IDs remain mandatory publication inputs; the documentation does not manufacture them.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/governance-and-responsibility

# Governance and Responsibility

How product, finance, security, custody, AI, risk and legal authority remain separated.

Good governance makes it impossible for one person to silently change the product, financial record, custody policy and public disclosure.

| Decision                | Responsible function          | Independent check                           |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Product terms and rates | Product + Finance             | Risk + Legal                                |
| Reward funding          | Treasury                      | Finance Control + Risk                      |
| Ledger policy           | Finance Engineering           | Financial Controller                        |
| Custody policy          | Treasury Operations           | Security + approval quorum                  |
| Contract upgrade        | Smart Contract Engineering    | Security review + timelock authority        |
| AI safety policy        | AI Product + Model Governance | Security + Legal/Risk                       |
| Incident reopening      | Incident Commander            | Finance, Security and accountable executive |
| Public claim            | Communications owner          | Evidence owner + Legal                      |

Committees publish a charter, membership by role, quorum, conflicts policy, minutes policy and escalation path.

## Segregation of duties

The role model prohibits toxic combinations such as code approval plus production deployment plus custody approval; reward-rate creation plus ledger posting; or AI policy change plus benchmark approval. Break-glass access is time-bound, independently approved and reviewed after use.

Every material decision produces a signed record with scope, evidence, dissent, residual risk, effective time and review date.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/risk-register

# Risk Register

How product, market, liquidity, custody, contract, operational and AI risks are governed.

The risk register connects every material risk to a product, asset, network, system and accountable role. It records likelihood, impact, leading indicator, limit, control, response and residual risk.

Risks are grouped into market, liquidity, network, protocol, smart-contract, custody, counterparty, financial, operational, cyber, privacy, regulatory, model and third-party families.

The user-facing product sheet shows only the risks relevant to that product. The full register preserves the technical detail and decision history.

## Limit breach

A limit breach emits a versioned risk event and selects a scoped action: monitor, restrict new positions, reduce capacity, switch provider, enter read-only mode, pause an affected operation, require manual reconciliation or wind down. The response has a deadline, approver and reopening test.

Residual risk cannot be accepted through an unowned note. Acceptance names the accountable authority, rationale, duration, compensating control and expiry.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/incident-response

# Incident Response

The exact operational states used when safety, availability or financial integrity is uncertain.

Whale CeFi does not treat every incident as the same outage. A problem can affect one asset, one network, one provider, one product or one capability while safe functions remain available.

| State          | What changes                                                                       |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Normal         | All authorised capabilities operate within limits.                                 |
| Degraded       | Safe reads continue; affected providers or writes are limited.                     |
| Read-only      | New financial instructions stop while balances and evidence remain visible.        |
| Scoped pause   | One affected asset, network, product or contract action stops.                     |
| Manual control | Named operators reconcile and approve bounded actions.                             |
| Recovery       | Root cause, balances and external settlement are verified before staged reopening. |

Every public notice states what is affected, what remains available, what users should do and when the next update appears.

## Authority and evidence

The incident record binds severity, commander, financial authority, custody authority, technical leads, communication owner, start time, evidence preservation, containment decisions and next-review time.

Reopening requires root-cause containment, ledger and settlement reconciliation, restored control evidence, independent approval and staged exposure. The post-incident record preserves the timeline, impact, corrective actions and due dates.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/service-status

# Service Status

Current capability state, dependency health, incident history and reconciliation condition.

The status page reports user journeys, not only server uptime. Deposits, plan opening, accrual display, withdrawals, account access, WENI, each supported network and each critical provider receive an independent state.

States are operational, degraded, read-only, scoped pause, maintenance or incident. Financial safety indicators show reconciliation condition and pending-age bands without exposing sensitive data.

Incident history remains available with start time, affected scope, user impact, updates, resolution and post-incident review.

## Status authority

Automated signals propose state; the incident workflow assigns owner and communication. Status data is signed by the service-status pipeline and sourced from journey SLOs, business invariants, provider health and reconciliation controls.

Scheduled maintenance lists affected capability, start and end window, rollback plan and next update. A missed update is itself visible.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/security-contact-and-disclosure

# Security Contact and Disclosure

How researchers and users report vulnerabilities, account compromise and suspected fraud.

Security reports use the published security channel and include the affected URL, contract, account surface or component; a reproducible description; impact; timestamps; and safe supporting material.

Do not include seed phrases, private keys, passwords, access tokens, unnecessary personal data or funds. Do not exploit other users, interrupt service or move assets to prove a finding.

The acknowledgement gives a case identifier, severity-triage window, safe communication route and next-update time. Urgent account compromise uses the dedicated authenticated support path.

The disclosure policy defines safe-harbour conditions, prohibited testing, in-scope assets, response targets, severity method, remediation validation, publication coordination and reward rules where applicable. Reports and artifacts are access-controlled and retained under the security evidence policy.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/glossary

# Glossary

Plain definitions for the words used across Whale CeFi product, finance, infrastructure and AI documentation.

| Term                | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Asset               | A digital token such as ETH, USDT or SOL.                                                                               |
| Network             | The blockchain route used to move an asset. The same symbol may exist on several networks.                              |
| Deposit             | An external transfer that becomes an available internal balance after validation and credit.                            |
| Flexible plan       | A plan without a fixed maturity date, governed by its closure and rate-change rules.                                    |
| Fixed-term plan     | A plan that remains committed until a named maturity date.                                                              |
| Monthly reward rate | A percentage defined for one month under the published day-count and accrual rules. It is not automatically APR or APY. |
| Accrual             | Reward earned over time before or while it is posted.                                                                   |
| Ledger              | The double-entry financial record of balances, obligations and movements.                                               |
| Reconciliation      | Comparing the internal ledger with custody, provider and blockchain evidence.                                           |
| Custody             | The system and policies that control cryptographic keys and asset movement.                                             |
| Smart contract      | Code deployed on a blockchain that executes defined rules.                                                              |
| Finality            | The point at which a network transaction is accepted as sufficiently irreversible under policy.                         |
| RPC                 | A service used to read blockchain state and send transactions.                                                          |
| Audit scope         | The exact code, commit, contract, network and date examined by an auditor.                                              |
| WENI                | the native intelligence system for Whale CeFi, the crypto-native intelligence and decision-support system.                             |
| Iron Boundary       | The separation that prevents probabilistic AI output from becoming final asset authority.                               |
| Provenance          | Where a fact came from, when it was observed and how it was validated.                                                  |

The machine-readable glossary is published as a stable JSON collection with unique identifiers and aliases. Definitions used in product terms take precedence over informal explanations when a legal or financial meaning differs.

# Technical References

Primary standards and specifications used by the canonical architecture.

The architecture uses standards as contracts, not as marketing badges. Conformance is claimed only for the functions and versions explicitly implemented and tested.

## Smart contracts and signing

* [ERC-20 Token Standard](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-20)
* [ERC-4626 Tokenized Vaults](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4626)
* [EIP-712 Typed Structured Data](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712)
* [ERC-1271 Contract Signature Validation](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1271)
* [OpenZeppelin Contracts](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts)
* [Safe Smart Account documentation](https://docs.safe.global/)

## Security and assurance

* [NIST Secure Software Development Framework, SP 800-218](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final)
* [NIST Security and Privacy Controls, SP 800-53 Rev. 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
* [OWASP Application Security Verification Standard](https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/)
* [OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/)

## Machine interfaces

* [JSON Schema Draft 2020-12](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12)

* [AsyncAPI Specification 3.1.0](https://www.asyncapi.com/docs/reference/specification/v3.1.0)

## AI governance

* [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
* [NIST Generative AI Profile](https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence)

External standards do not replace the Whale CeFi product, financial, risk, or authority invariants defined in this documentation.

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/developers-and-reference/change-history

# Change History

A chronological record of product, calculation, contract, policy, audit and documentation changes.

The changelog records every material change with effective date, affected pages and registries, previous version, new version, reason, approver and migration impact.

Change classes include product terms, rate schedule, supported asset or network, calculation method, contract deployment, audit or finding status, custody policy, legal perimeter, AI capability, privacy rule and documentation correction.

Historical URLs remain valid. A superseded page points to its replacement and explains the effective interval.

## Release discipline

Documentation changes are reviewed with the product or system change that makes them necessary. A feature cannot be promoted without its terms, risk disclosure, registry record, help path and change entry. Emergency corrections record the incident or evidence that triggered them.

# Legal and Support

This section identifies the organisations behind Whale CeFi, the customer’s legal relationship, asset rights, service eligibility, privacy perimeter, risk disclosures, complaints process, and official contact routes.

Whale CeFi is the product brand. **Whale Foundation**, officially registered
in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, is the current stewardship and
intellectual-property entity. Customer-facing financial services are mapped
to the applicable Whale CeFi operating entity in the Entity and Service
Register.

The separation is intentional: brand stewardship, software ownership, customer contracting, custody, treasury, and regulated obligations are not collapsed into one vague word such as “platform.”

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/entity-and-service-register

# Entity and Service Register

Whale CeFi uses an explicit service map so the user can identify which legal person is responsible for each capability.

## Current group perimeter

| Entity | Location | Role | What it does not do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whale Foundation — officially registered | Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates | Brand and IP stewardship, governance constitution, research and ecosystem oversight | Does not silently replace the customer’s contracting entity |
| Whale CeFi Services Ltd | Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates | Customer agreement, product operation, account and service responsibility | Does not treat customer principal as company revenue |
| Whale CeFi Custody SPV Ltd | Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates | Segregated custody and settlement perimeter under the approved custody model | Does not originate discretionary product terms |

The authoritative corporate record holds the exact legal form, registration
number, registered address, authority information, permission scope, official
register reference, service mapping, governing law, complaints route, and
effective date. This public documentation states the approved entity map
without reproducing restricted corporate identifiers.

## Service mapping

The plan review identifies the exact contracting entity before confirmation. A change of contracting entity, custody model, governing law, or insolvency treatment is material and creates a new terms version. It cannot be applied silently to an existing locked position.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/customer-relationship-and-asset-rights

# Customer Relationship and Asset Rights

The legal state of an asset changes only through a clearly disclosed product event.

## Before a plan opens

A credited asset remains in the custody state defined by the Client Agreement. The user can see whether legal title, beneficial ownership, segregation, and withdrawal rights remain with the user.

## When an earning position opens

The review states whether the arrangement is custody, agency, lending, or another legally approved relationship; whether title remains with the customer or transfers; how assets may be used; pooling and segregation; rehypothecation; counterparties; insurance; insolvency treatment; claim priority; loss allocation; and exit rights.

No page uses “your assets remain yours” as a universal slogan if the earning contract creates a creditor relationship.

## Product consent object

The accepted record contains product version, contracting entity, asset identity, principal, legal position, permitted use, reward obligation, maturity, exit rules, risk version, terms hash, timestamp, and user confirmation.

## Insolvency and loss

CeFi earning products are not bank deposits and are not protected by deposit insurance unless a specific verified policy says otherwise. Depending on the legal arrangement, the customer can become a secured or unsecured creditor and can lose some or all principal and expected reward.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/eligibility-and-geographic-access

# Eligibility and Geographic Access

Availability is determined by the intersection of customer type, country, entity, product classification, asset, network, sanctions policy, verification state, and operational capability.

The website, onboarding, application, API, documentation, and Client Agreement read from the same versioned eligibility matrix. If the matrix denies a capability, the interface does not merely display a disclaimer; it blocks the operation.

## Eligibility states

Available, limited, professional-only, institutional-only, temporarily suspended, unsupported, and legally prohibited are distinct. A service can be available in one country through one entity and unavailable elsewhere.

WENI can explain the published rule and gather information. It cannot make the final eligibility decision or override a deterministic deny result.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/risk-disclosure

# Risk Disclosure

You can lose some or all of your principal and any expected reward. Whale CeFi earning products are not bank deposits and are not covered by deposit insurance unless an exact verified policy explicitly states otherwise.

## Material risk classes

- platform insolvency and creditor recovery;
- counterparty, custodian, borrower, or strategy default;
- stablecoin depeg, issuer freeze, or redemption restriction;
- concentration, correlation, leverage, liquidation, and slashing;
- rehypothecation and encumbrance;
- liquidity queues, delayed exits, and suspended routes;
- smart-contract exploit, admin compromise, and oracle failure;
- blockchain congestion, reorganisation, bridge, validator, and finality risk;
- account takeover, fraud, operational error, and reconciliation failure;
- legal, sanctions, tax, and geographic-access change;
- conflicts of interest and related-party exposure;
- WENI error, stale evidence, or misunderstood output.

Each risk record names the owner, indicator, limit, trigger, control, residual risk, customer impact, legal loss allocation, recovery priority, review date, and jurisdiction-specific wording.

Controls reduce probability or impact. They do not make loss impossible.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/privacy-and-data-protection

# Privacy and Data Protection

Whale CeFi separates account, verification, financial, blockchain, security, progression, support, analytics, and WENI data by purpose and authority.

The Privacy Notice identifies controller, processing purpose, legal basis, categories, recipients, subprocessors, processing regions, retention, security measures, automated decision involvement, user rights, contact route, and effective version.

## WENI-specific boundary

Private account context is retrieved only for an authorised purpose and minimum scope. Screenshots and voice inputs use an isolated ephemeral processing path unless the user expressly saves an item. Secrets and seed phrases are blocked from memory. Financial authority records are not editable through conversational memory.

## Rights

The data-rights route supports access, correction, deletion where legally available, restriction, objection, portability, consent withdrawal, and complaint. Identity verification is proportional to the sensitivity of the request.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/complaints-and-appeals

# Complaints and Appeals

A complaint is different from general support, a security incident, a fraud report, an account-restriction appeal, or a privacy request. Each route has a distinct owner and response clock.

## Complaint record

The user receives a case ID, acknowledgement, issue summary, requested remedy, evidence channel, accountable entity, target response time, escalation status, final response, and external escalation route where applicable.

The complaint reviewer can correct service decisions within authority but cannot rewrite blockchain history, invent reserve evidence, suppress an incident, or mark an audit finding closed without the required proof.

## Appeals

Progression, eligibility, fraud, and account restrictions use their own review rules. A final outcome explains the applied rule and effective remedy to the extent permitted by security, privacy, and law.

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/contact-routes

# Contact Routes

Use the route that matches the issue. Do not rely on unsolicited direct messages, Telegram administrators, or addresses on a non-canonical domain.

| Situation | Official route | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Account compromise | Authenticated emergency support or account-compromise form | Freeze and recovery workflow with urgent case ID |
| Security vulnerability | security@whale-cefi.com and the disclosure form | Triage, safe-harbour policy, encrypted evidence route |
| Fraud or scam | Dedicated fraud report | Evidence intake and case tracking |
| Formal complaint | Complaints form and published postal/email route | Acknowledgement, final response, escalation |
| Privacy request | Privacy contact | Identity-verified rights workflow |
| General support | Help Centre ticket | Searchable guidance and case ID |

Whale CeFi never asks for a seed phrase, private key, remote desktop access, or transfer to a “safe wallet.”

The repository includes an RFC 9116-compatible [security.txt](../public/.well-known/security.txt).

---

SOURCE: https://docs.whale-cefi.com/legal-and-support/document-and-terms-control

# Document and Terms Control

Every material document has an identifier, version, effective time, owner, approval scope, hash, superseded version, and change summary.

Material changes include contracting entity, product classification, asset rights, custody model, rate nature, calculation method, fees, early exit, maturity, supported network, risk allocation, privacy purpose, WENI authority, and dispute route.

Locked positions retain the accepted product and terms version unless a lawfully permitted emergency or user-approved migration expressly applies. Flexible-plan changes affect only accrual beginning at the disclosed effective time after the disclosed effective time.

Documentation corrections that do not change legal or economic meaning remain traceable but do not create a new product version.
